newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Dissidents urge for free access to Algeria's media.
newsitem.headline: Dissidents urge for free access to Algeria's media.

text.p: Algeria's main secular opposition party on Saturday urged President Liamine Zeroual to allow all political parties to express views through state-run media on the expected constitutional referendum.

In a letter to Zeroual, the Socialist Forces Front (FFS) said "to guarantee the credibility of the popular consultation and its transparency...free access to the public television and radio should be allowed to all parties."
Reuters received a copy of the letter after a meeting in Algiers of the FFS leadership on Saturday. The party did not specify which parties were banned from the state-run media.
Algerian officials were not immediately available for comment.
The FFS also wants "the immediate official announcement of the referendum campaign...and that the integral neutrality of the administration in the polls be guaranteed."

Algerian authorities started a campaign in October to win support for a new constitution, to be put to a referendum at the end of November, which increases the powers of the president but limits him to two five-year terms.
The draft underlined Zeroual's bid to establish a multiparty democracy built around a strong president to pull Algeria out of nearly five years of civil strife.
It gives Algerians the right for the first time since the country's independence in 1962 to found political parties, subject to the ban on Islamic parties and other founding principles.
Algeria erupted into violence early in 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were poised to win. More than 50,000 people have since died.
Many Algerians blame the central power for allowing the now outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) to dominate politics in violation of a law banning religion-based movements from seeking to govern.
Algeria's radical secular opponents, including the FFS, have threatened to tell supporters to boycott the poll on a new constitutiton if their demands are not satisfied.
